variants.headline: Our network in {{civilization}} holds the policy threshold
body: Our network at the court of {{civilization}} now holds at least 200 points. The service counts {{points}} there. At that level, policy choices made at that court can reach our foreign office, and the reports come from clerks and table companions rather than from public announcements. A choice argued in a closed room can now find its way to us.

variants.headline: What is the listening in {{civilization}} for?
body: Our network in {{civilization}} holds at least 200 points, and policy choices made at that court can now reach our foreign office. The {{terms.civic.government}} should say what it means to do with what it hears. A network that listens and never acts is an expense with a good name. Let the ministers report what the last season of listening bought the country.

variants.headline: Our network in {{civilization}} holds the treaty threshold
body: Our network at the court of {{civilization}} now holds at least 800 points. Private treaties between that court and another government reach us only when our network at the other party's court is also at least 800. On this side of the arrangement the ground is ready, and no text has arrived through this alone.

variants.headline: The groundwork for reading {{civilization}}'s treaties
body: Our network at the court of {{civilization}} now holds at least 800 points. A private treaty between that court and another signatory becomes readable to us only when our people at both capitals each hold a network at that level. The mission at {{civilization}} has done its part; the other party's court must still match it.

variants.headline: The vote in {{cityState}} went our way
body: {{cityState}} has voted the way we hoped. The count was read from the town hall steps, and the candidate we backed stood in the square below, shaking every hand offered. The friends we helped now hold the seats that decide which envoy is heard first.

variants.headline: The vote in {{cityState}} went against us
body: Our money went into an election in {{cityState}} and came back as receipts. The count turned against us before midnight, and the man we opposed thanked his voters from a balcony. Whoever answers for this should explain why the town preferred the other candidate.

variants.headline: The election in {{cityState}} goes our way
body: Letters from {{cityState}} confirm that the contest there closed in favor of the candidate our {{terms.civic.government}} thought worth backing. The council house steps are swept and empty this morning, and the clerks within are tying the campaign's papers into bundles. Traders from that quarter may expect a friendlier reception at our gates for years to come.

variants.headline: Make the case for meddling in {{cityState}}
body: Good coin went to {{cityState}} to buy an election, and the election stayed unbought! Let the minister who signed for the purse name one advantage an honest envoy could not have won. If there is none, the next purse should stay shut and the voters there should be left in peace.

variants.headline: One number from {{cityState}}'s murky business
body: One number out of {{cityState}} is worth more than all the speeches: our standing there shifted by {{influence|point|points}}. Agents will go on arguing which favors were bought and which promises were merely made. The figure stands in the ledger, and every request we make in that town will be measured against it.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} adopts {{policy}}
body: {{civilization}} has adopted {{policy}} as its guiding policy. The proclamation was read at the court this week, and the clerks have begun copying the new instructions into the registers. Its neighbors will feel the change first in the tone of its envoys.

variants.headline: Our envoy is at the court that adopted {{policy}}
body: Our envoy is posted at the court of {{civilization}}, where {{policy}} has been adopted. The court has said little beyond the words of the policy. A policy is a promise about where a nation will spend its money and its patience, and our mission there will watch where this one leads.

variants.headline: From abroad: {{civilization}} turns to {{policy}}
body: Letters from {{civilization}} relate that the court has chosen {{policy}} for its policy. In our counting houses, brokers who trade on that frontier read the news twice and asked what it means for the price of carriage. Every chancellery that keeps a file on that court will read the change the same way.

variants.headline: A new policy in {{civilization}}, and no word here
body: {{civilization}} has taken up {{policy}}, and our {{terms.civic.government}} has offered the country nothing but silence. A policy is a promise about where a nation will spend its money and its patience. The {{terms.civic.people}} should hear from our own ministers what this one means for the roads and treaties we share.

variants.headline: Our envoys obtain the treaty between {{from}} and {{to}}
body: A copy of the treaty between {{from}} and {{to}} has reached our foreign office. The clauses are written out in full, and the copy is filed with the rest of the season's dispatches. The text came to us through our own people rather than through any messenger of the two courts.

variants.headline: The terms between {{from}} and {{to}}
body: {{from}} gives: {{fromGives}}.
{{to}} gives: {{toGives}}.
Both courts signed, and our copy came by our own road.

variants.headline: What {{from}} put into the treaty with {{to}}
body: {{from}} gives: {{fromGives}}.
{{to}} gave nothing in the recorded terms, so the deal was one-sided.

variants.headline: What {{to}} put into the treaty with {{from}}
body: {{to}} gives: {{toGives}}.
{{from}} gave nothing in the recorded terms, so the deal was one-sided.

variants.headline: What {{from}} and {{to}} bought from each other
body: The treaty between {{from}} and {{to}} is now in our hands, and it answers the question the chanceries have been asking. Each side gave something it could spare for something it wanted more. The balance of the exchange will show in the next season of their trade and their quarrels.

variants.headline: The {{from}} and {{to}} treaty, as we have it
body: Our envoys have obtained the treaty between {{from}} and {{to}}. Both courts signed it, and our foreign office holds a copy of the terms.

variants.headline: Our diplomat takes up post in {{civilization}}
body: An envoy of ours now keeps a post in {{civilization}}. His trunks went into the coach before first light, and the dispatch case rode on the seat beside him. Letters to that court will no longer wait on a willing traveler.

variants.headline: An envoy established at {{capital}}
body: In this year the court of {{civilization}} admitted our envoy at {{capital}}. The porters were paid their customary fees, and a first letter went home within the week. The practice of stationing a voice abroad, kept by our fathers, is thus maintained.

variants.headline: A diplomat goes to {{civilization}}
body: In {{civilization}} tonight, our envoy has taken his post. He will dine at their table and listen to every toast. One ear in that hall is worth a regiment, and the treasury pays a fraction for it.

variants.headline: Our diplomat leaves {{civilization}}
body: Our envoy has left the court of {{civilization}}. The post stands empty, and letters to that capital will now travel by courier and wait on whatever welcome the road provides.

variants.headline: Our envoy quits {{civilization}} as the war goes on
body: Our envoy has left {{civilization}} while the war continues. The post stands empty, and any letters to that capital now wait on the road. Whatever the mission gathered before it closed is with the foreign office.

variants.headline: The mission to {{civilization}} closes
body: Our envoy has left the court of {{civilization}}, and the two countries remain at peace. The post stands empty. A post left empty is still a door, and either court may knock again.

variants.headline: The envoy departs from {{civilization}}
body: In this season our envoy left the court of {{civilization}}, and the mission was closed. The rooms he kept stand empty. The record notes the departure and leaves the reason unstated.

variants.headline: A foreign spy, caught and named
body: Our officers took a foreign agent inside our borders, and the documents on him carried the mark of the service that sent him. The magistrate studied the seal a second time before he reached for wax. A formal protest is on its way to that court, where it will be denied in equally formal language.

variants.headline: A foreign spy is killed in our streets
body: Our watch killed a foreign spy inside our borders this week, and he was buried before the sun rose. Our {{terms.civic.government}} has traced him to the service that employed him, though his people at home will hear only of a death abroad. The watch keeps the rest of the matter sealed.

variants.headline: Hear it! A spy is taken in {{cityName}}
body: {{cityName}}, attend, {{terms.civic.people}}! A stranger came among you to pry into your affairs, and the watch laid hands on him before he finished. Held fast! Go back to your suppers; the watch does not sleep.

variants.headline: A foreign spy uncovered!
body: Neighbors, a foreign spy was pulled off our streets by the watch last night! The ministry has the service's name in a drawer and means to keep it there. Ask your alderman why the people who live here are told of such things only after the danger has gone.

variants.headline: The spy is identified as an agent of {{culprit}}
body: The agent unmasked inside our borders was working for {{culprit}}. The papers found with him carried that court's mark, and the magistrate read the seal before he reached for the wax. The foreign office has the name in writing now, and {{culprit}} will be asked to explain what the seal was doing on a stranger's papers.

variants.headline: Demand an answer from {{culprit}}
body: {{culprit}} sent a spy into our country, and the {{terms.civic.government}} has sent a note. A note is what a chancery writes when it hopes the matter will end there. Let the foreign office demand the agent's handler, name the office that paid him, and publish the answer if one comes.

variants.headline: {{culprit}} has been named before
body: Earlier reports in this period have named {{culprit}} as well. Our service counts {{earlier|earlier report|earlier reports}} naming the same civilization, and the same agent can appear in more than one of them. Whether our government has answered those reports is not recorded here.

variants.headline: Seen at the work, but not named
body: One of our people abroad was seen where he should not have been. Nobody there has yet tied him to us, and no protest has arrived at our embassy. The local watch is questioning porters at the ministry gate while our staff keeps to its ordinary routine.

variants.headline: What {{target}} may hold back
body: In {{target}} the authorities are certain a spy was at work and cannot say for whom. That uncertainty spares our envoy a formal protest this month. The bill will be paid in small coin: documents opened twice, familiar faces asked for papers, and our visitors in {{target}} kept standing in hallways. Someone in the ministry should explain how a trained agent came to be spotted.

variants.headline: Our spy drew notice and may bring home {{possibleTechnology}}
body: Word from our embassy says the agent was spotted in the course of his work, and the reports do not settle whether {{possibleTechnology}} came home with him. Officials there have spent the week asking after strangers who called at odd hours. Should the papers he carried prove sound, the alarm will look like a bargain.

variants.headline: One of ours is marked in {{cityName}}
body: In this season a man of ours was observed at his task in {{cityName}}. The watch questioned the gatekeepers for an afternoon and then let the affair drop. Whether he left with anything of value, this record does not say.

variants.headline: A foreign spy, seen and unnamed
body: Our watchers have spotted a foreign agent plying his trade within our borders. Nobody has yet named his employer, and the streets around the embassies have turned strangely quiet. Extra patrols will walk the watch house rounds until the question is settled.

variants.headline: The spy who died unnamed
body: A foreign spy died at the hands of our watchers, and he carried no name for the man who paid him. His body was removed before the stalls opened. Somewhere a handler now waits for a message that cannot be sent, and to ask after it would expose him.

variants.headline: Notice: the watch is awake
body: Be it known that a foreign agent has been observed at his work within our borders, and that his master remains unidentified. The {{terms.civic.government}} requests that householders note unfamiliar callers and speak of this matter to no one outside the household until the inquiry closes.

variants.headline: Someone was watching {{cityName}}
body: A stranger with quick eyes was working {{cityName}} this week, and he did not come from any house on our street. He was a foreign spy, and no one can name the man who hired him. The market still sold its bread, but every unfamiliar face at a stall got a long look.

variants.headline: Our agent reports the work in {{city}}
body: Our agent in {{city}} sends word of the city's next work. The workshops of {{civilization}} have taken up {{production}}, and the market talks of little else. The agent will keep his place by the window and count what comes and goes.

variants.headline: {{production}} in {{city}} with {{turnsLeft}} to run
body: Word from our agent in {{city}} names {{production}} as the work now under way there. At the current rate the city has {{turnsLeft}} left before it is finished. That is an estimate, not an official schedule, and the agent will report whether the work finishes on that count.

variants.headline: The complaint our agent hears in {{city}}
body: Our agent in {{city}} writes that the complaint he hears most often is {{unrest}}. The queues at the market are longer than they were, and the guards at the gate no longer argue with the people who wait. He does not call the city close to open trouble, only changed.

variants.headline: Hunger in {{city}}, as our agent tells it
body: Our agent in {{city}} reports that the city's food reserves are running low and that it loses food each turn. The bakers sell what flour they have by the handful, and families from the outer streets walk in to look for bread. He will write again when the markets change.

variants.headline: Named abroad, and the doors close
body: A foreign government has put a name to one of our agents, and the name is the right one. Our embassy heard the news before the official note reached its door, which says something about the leaks on that side. The cipher he used is ash in the grate this morning.

variants.headline: Killed abroad, and known to them
body: One of our agents died in service abroad this week, and the government that killed him knows who he worked for. At the ministry a clerk closed the file with a single stroke of the pen and said nothing. What he was doing there will remain inside those walls.

variants.headline: Our spy is killed abroad, unnamed
body: A man of ours was killed abroad, and the men who killed him never learned whose errand he ran. No protest will be lodged, and no name will appear in print. The service will keep the loss to itself and leave the file shut.

variants.headline: The ministry owes us its account
body: {{target}} has named one of our agents in public, and our ministry has not offered a word in reply. That silence asks the country to trust a foreign account, and a country that pays for a secret service deserves better. Let the minister say what good the operation did. The agent's name can stay out of the answer.

variants.headline: The cost of the quiet work in {{target}}
body: Our agent died in {{target}}, and the men who buried him knew which flag he served. The price of such work comes in two parts: the life lost, and the goodwill with {{target}} that goes with it. What the service gained in exchange, nobody outside its doors can say. The country should demand an answer before another name is spent.

variants.headline: A winter coat passed on
body: He died abroad in the service of his country, doing the work he had been given. At the rooms where he lodged, the landlady handed his heavy coat to a traveler, remembering how he had once done the same for a man caught in the rain. The service keeps its own account of his name.

variants.headline: Our spy may have gained {{possibleTechnology}}
body: Our spy finished his work abroad and slipped out without raising an alarm. Early word from the service says {{possibleTechnology}} may have come home with him. Should the reports prove true, our workshops will show the difference before the season changes.

variants.headline: The quiet account
body: Entered in the ledger of the service:
Watchmen roused: none. Goods carried home, report unverified: {{possibleTechnology}}.
On the other side of the page: the long years of study we may have saved.

variants.headline: Unnoticed in {{target}}
body: In {{target}} tonight, our people finished their work and no bell rang. The service believes the night's take may include {{possibleTechnology}}. If so, the gap in learning between our two nations has narrowed by a stride. Neither country's workshops will be told the reason.

variants.headline: Quiet win: possibly {{possibleTechnology}}
body: No alarm. No witness. Probable prize: {{possibleTechnology}}. Short report, good reading.

variants.headline: One of ours has taken rooms in {{city}}
body: One of our quiet people has settled into {{city}}, a city of {{civilization}}. The room he rents above a shop looks down on the gate and opens onto a back stair. The {{owner.civic.government}} keeps its own hours, and he intends to learn every one.

variants.headline: A quiet posting to {{city}}
body: Notice is given that a trusted servant of ours has taken a place in {{city}}, a city of {{civilization}}. Correspondence sent along the usual road will find him. His first letter home will describe those parts of the city that visitors are never invited to see.

variants.headline: One of ours goes to {{city}}
body: They say a quiet man of ours has gone down the road to {{city}}, in the land of {{civilization}}. He will keep a stall in that market, and the gate will learn his face. When the wind shifts, word will come back along the same road.

variants.headline: A room inside {{city}}
body: From a window in {{city}}, our agent sees what no dispatch from {{civilization}} will ever admit. He counts the wagons at the gate each morning, and the tally tells him what {{civilization}} is moving before any announcement. The question is whether that traffic is ordinary trade or the supplies for a road being built in secret. Either answer is worth the rent.

variants.headline: Spy season: {{merge.values.operations|report|reports}} from our cities
body: Foreign agents were busy this season. {{merge.values.operations|report|reports}} reached this office from our cities, and every one of them began with a stranger found where he did not belong.
The watch should keep its own count. A season like this one is a warning that someone across the border has decided our affairs are worth the risk.

variants.headline: A diplomat of {{civilization}} arrives at our capital
body: A diplomat from {{civilization}} has moved into a house near our capital's ministry. The gatekeeper has one more face to learn and one more name for the visitors' book. Matters that once waited on a courier can now be raised at a door.

variants.headline: An envoy from {{civilization}} at our court
body: It is with satisfaction that we note the arrival of an envoy from {{civilization}} at our capital. The reception ledger has a new page, and his name is written there in ink not yet dry. A message carried by a diplomat arrives with fewer bruises than one carried by rumor, and honest words are welcome at this court.

variants.headline: A listener at our table
body: {{civilization}} has planted an envoy in our capital, and we should count the cost of courtesy. Wine is cheap; an unlocked study is not. Let the steward pour freely and let the clerks lock every drawer before the guest arrives. A visitor who knows he is watched writes a careful report, and a careful report serves his masters poorly.

variants.headline: The envoy of {{civilization}} leaves our capital
body: The envoy of {{civilization}} has left our capital. His house near the ministry is shuttered, and the visitors' book has been closed on his last page. Matters that could be raised at his door will now wait on a courier.

variants.headline: A guest departs: the envoy of {{civilization}}
body: We are informed that the envoy of {{civilization}} has taken his leave of our capital, and the gate log records the hour. We wish him a safe road and a short absence.

variants.headline: Why did the envoy of {{civilization}} go home?
body: The envoy of {{civilization}} has left our capital, and the {{terms.civic.government}} has not said why. A mission is not called home without a reason, and the reason is usually a message. Let the foreign office tell the country what passed before the door closed.

variants.headline: The envoy of {{civilization}} takes his leave
body: In this season the envoy of {{civilization}} departed our capital, and the house he kept stands empty. He came with letters and left with letters, as envoys have done in every reign this record remembers. The gatekeeper noted the hour and nothing more.
